reference: Parity cases use the installed e2fsprogs lsattr (man page: 1.47.2), executed by system Bash inside the submit helper mandatory private namespaces. Candidate cases use the locally rebuilt Bash with empty PATH. Raw stdout bytes, independently checked reference statuses, stderr policy, and fixture trees are compared; no output sorting or flag-field normalization is performed. Type/help cases use independent Bash metadata contracts and do not count as operation coverage.
coverage: Complete 22-column short flag field on ordinary fixture files/directories; no flags are set.
End of options, leading-dash path, no operands, directory-only mode and combined -daR.
-a includes hidden names and . and ..; dot-directory queries stay inside private fixture trees.
-R includes child headings, leading/trailing separators, empty directories, nested siblings and hidden directories without dot recursion.
Symlinks to files/directories and dangling symlinks as explicit operands; unsupported symlink entries diagnosed during a successful directory walk.
Missing/multiple operands preserve failure statuses and continue processing.
Bash type/help metadata contracts, recorded separately from operation coverage.
exclusions: Setting nonzero inode attribute bits is deferred because immutable/append flags can obstruct cleanup and the fixture filesystem does not guarantee writable ext4 flags.
No block device, host path, real filesystem mount, or privileged inode mutation is used.
Attribute-bit mappings on a disposable ext4 filesystem or controlled ioctl mock remain unqualified.
Full option parity (-V, -l, -p, -v), option permutation and exact diagnostic wording are outside this repair.

Directory iteration order is filesystem-dependent: raw comparisons retain the local reference order, and portability review must distinguish independent directory ordering from missing columns, entries, headings or blank lines.

The added nonzero bit constants come from factual Linux inode flag definitions and documented CLI letters; active-bit rendering beyond naturally present e remains deferred to a controlled mock or disposable VM.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash resolves lsattr as a builtin in the pinned candidate.
Confirm Bash has a nonempty help topic registered for lsattr.
cases.script:
help lsattr > help.txt
[[ -s help.txt ]]
printf 'help available\n'

cases.purpose: Compare the basic attribute line and status for a small relative regular file.
Check that -- allows a relative operand whose name begins with a dash.
Check -d reports the directory operand itself instead of walking its entries.
Check the no-operand default directory walk and omission of dot-prefixed entries.
Check -a includes dot-prefixed directory entries while walking a relative directory. Run in a child fixture directory so . and .. both name private fixture directories.
cases.script:
mkdir scope
cd scope
printf 'visible\n' > visible
printf 'hidden\n' > .hidden
lsattr -a .

cases.purpose: Compare recursive traversal over a small nested tree containing one file at each level.
cases.script:
mkdir tree
mkdir tree/sub
printf 'root\n' > tree/root
printf 'nested\n' > tree/sub/item
lsattr -R tree

cases.purpose: Check GNU's unsupported-attribute result for a relative symlink to a regular-file target.
cases.script:
printf 'target\n' > target
ln -s target link
lsattr -- link

cases.purpose: Check nonzero status and a diagnostic for a missing relative operand.
Reject a symlink to a directory as an explicit operand without traversing it.
cases.script:
mkdir target
printf 'inside\n' > target/item
ln -s target link
lsattr -R -- link

cases.purpose: Reject a dangling symlink as an explicit operand.
A directory walk diagnoses unsupported symlink entries without following them, and still exits zero; recursive output preserves headings, separators, and native directory order.
cases.script:
mkdir tree
printf 'data\n' > tree/plain
mkdir tree/sub
ln -s plain tree/file-link
ln -s sub tree/dir-link
ln -s missing tree/dangling
lsattr -R tree

cases.purpose: Combined -aR must display dot directories without recursing into . or ..; a child directory keeps every read inside the private fixture tree.
cases.script:
mkdir scope
mkdir scope/tree
mkdir scope/tree/.hidden-dir
printf 'nested\n' > scope/tree/.hidden-dir/item
lsattr -aR scope/tree

cases.purpose: Preserve failure status while continuing across a missing operand, a regular file, and a directory operand.
cases.script:
printf 'data\n' > plain
mkdir tree
printf 'child\n' > tree/item
lsattr -- missing plain tree

cases.purpose: Retain recursive headings, blank lines, and native directory iteration order for empty and nested sibling directories.
cases.script:
mkdir tree
mkdir tree/z
mkdir tree/a
mkdir tree/a/deeper
printf 'tail\n' > tree/tail
lsattr -R tree

cases.purpose: -d takes precedence over -R and -a for explicit directory operands and preserves multiple operand order.
cases.script:
mkdir tree
printf 'ignored\n' > tree/item
printf 'data\n' > plain
lsattr -daR tree plain .

cases.purpose: Qualify exact flag-letter mapping and order for enabled inode attributes.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable ext4 VM/image with controlled inode-flag setup, or a reviewed ioctl mock that returns deterministic FS_IOC_GETFLAGS values, plus an independent e2fsprogs oracle. Future coverage should exercise every supported bit, unset bits, and the full GNU flag field, with teardown that cannot leave immutable or append-only state behind.
